speaker: Sam
text: Maya, are we ready for the community food collection? Look at Alex by the door. He is sitting alone with a notebook. He looks bored.

speaker: Maya
text: He might simply be concentrating. Being quiet does not always mean someone is bored.

speaker: Sam
text: That is possible, but he has not spoken to anyone. Do you know him?

speaker: Maya
text: Yes. This is his first time volunteering. He told me he is checking the guest list and trying to learn everyone’s names.

speaker: Sam
text: Oh, that changes my impression. And you must be tired. You have been working since six this morning.

speaker: Maya
text: A little. At first, I felt confused because the instructions were confusing. But we organized the supplies together, so I feel calmer now.

speaker: Sam
text: What about that poster? It says, Coffee cups demand a holiday. That can’t be a real news report.

speaker: Maya
text: It is satire. Cups cannot ask for holidays. The joke exaggerates how busy we have been preparing everything.

speaker: Sam
text: I see. The poster is funny, although the work is tiring. Shall I invite Alex to help us with the boxes?

speaker: Maya
text: Good idea. A friendly question can help break the ice. Ask him what he enjoys doing.

speaker: Sam
text: I will. I thought he was not interested, but now I want to hear his story.

speaker: Maya
text: Exactly. Notice the clues, consider another explanation, and talk to the person before you decide.
